_note: Hand-translated English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Shemot 4 (Moses' three signs, speech impediment, Aaron appointed, return to Egypt, Zipporah circumcision, meeting Aaron, people believe). Saadia-distinctive moves: v.2 מנבהא = 'prompting him' (Saadia adds the participle — God's question is pedagogical); v.6 ביצ'א כאלת'לג = 'white as snow' — Saadia RATIONALIZES away from disease: the Hebrew מצרעת (leprous) is replaced by simple 'white' (the visible sign, not the medical condition); v.10 ד'ו נטק = 'a man of speech' (for איש דברים); v.10 ת'קיל אלפם ואלסאן = 'heavy of mouth and tongue'; v.11 nominal series of mute/deaf/seeing/blind preserves Saadia's tetrad; v.14 פאשתד וגד אללה עליה = 'And God was greatly angered with him' (Saadia's anti-anthropomorphic for חרה אף — no literal 'nose burned', just 'was angered'); v.14 אלליואני = 'the Levite'; v.14 יסר פי קלבה = 'rejoice in his heart'; v.16 תרגמאנא = 'a translator/spokesman' (Saadia for לפה — Aaron will be Moses' interpreter); v.16 אסתאדא = 'a master' — CRITICAL anti-anthropomorphic move: Saadia REFUSES to render the Hebrew 'אלהים' here as 'god' (you shall be to him as God); substitutes 'a master/sustainer' to avoid implying Moses becomes divine for Aaron; v.17 אלמעגזאת = 'the wonders / miraculous signs'; v.18 הל הם באקון = 'whether they are still surviving'; v.20 ארכבהם עלי' חמיר = 'set them upon donkeys'; v.21 אלבראהין = 'the proofs / demonstrations' (Saadia's word for המפתים); v.21 אשדד קלבה = 'I shall harden his heart' (Saadia preserves the divine causation here, not softening); v.22 כד'א קאל אללה משרפא = 'Thus says God, in honor/glorification' (Saadia adds משרפא — God speaks with elevated dignity over Israel); v.22 אבני בכרי = 'My son, My firstborn'; v.24 פי אלמבית = 'at the lodging-place'; v.24 פאגא ולדה = 'came suddenly upon his son' (Saadia interprets the cryptic Hebrew ויפגשהו יהוה as the angel meeting the SON, not Moses — solving the longstanding interpretive crux about who is attacked); v.25 צואנא = 'a flint'; v.25 כאד אלערוס אן יכון מקתולא = 'the bridegroom [the boy] was about to be killed' (Saadia interprets חתן דמים as 'bridegroom marked for blood/death'); v.26 צאר אלערוס אלמקתול מכ'תונא = 'the bridegroom marked for death has become circumcised' — Saadia resolves the cryptic verse: through circumcision the child was saved; v.27 וקבלה = 'and he kissed him' (cognate); v.31 ד'כר אללה = 'God has remembered'; v.31 ונצ'ר לצ'עפהם = 'and He has looked upon their affliction'.

translations.1: And Moses replied and said: 'Perhaps they will not believe me, and will not accept from me; rather they will say: God did not appear to you.'
translations.2: And God said to him, prompting him: 'What is this in your hand?' He said: 'A staff.'
translations.3: He said: 'Throw it upon the ground.' And he threw it, and it became a serpent; and Moses fled from before it.
translations.4: God said to him: 'Stretch out your hand and seize its tail.' And he stretched out his hand and seized it, and it became a staff in his hand.
translations.5: So that they may believe that God — the God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — has appeared to you.
translations.6: And He said to him further: 'Put your hand into your bosom.' And he put it in; then he brought it out — and behold, it was white as snow.
translations.7: And He said: 'Return your hand to your bosom.' And he returned it; then he brought it out, and it had returned [to be] like the rest of his body.
translations.8: And if they will not believe you, and will not accept the first sign, then they will believe the second sign.
translations.9: And if they will not believe these two signs, and will not accept from you — then take from the water of the Nile, and pour it upon the dry ground; and it shall change, and shall become blood upon the dry ground.'
translations.10: And Moses said to his Lord: 'O my Lord, I am not a man of speech — neither from yesterday and before, nor from the time You spoke to Your servant; for I am heavy of mouth and of tongue together.'
translations.11: God said to him: 'Who made speech for the human? Or who makes the mute, or the deaf, or the seeing, or the blind? Is it not I, God?
translations.12: And now, go — and I shall be with your speech, and shall direct you in what you shall say.'
translations.13: He said: 'O my Lord — send by whomever You will send.'
translations.14: And God was greatly angered with him, and said: 'Is not Aaron your brother the Levite? I know that he is a speaker; and behold, he is going out to meet you, and he will see you, and rejoice in his heart.
translations.15: And you shall speak to him, and shall set the words in his mouth; and I shall be with your speech and with his speech, and shall direct you in what you shall do.
translations.16: And he shall speak for you to the people; and he shall be to you a spokesman, and you shall be to him a master.
translations.17: And take this staff in your hand — you shall perform the wonders by it.'
translations.18: And Moses went, and returned to Jether his father-in-law, and said to him: 'Let me go and return to my brothers who are in Egypt, and see whether they are still surviving.' Jethro said to him: 'Go in peace.'
translations.19: Then God said to Moses in Midian: 'Go, return to Egypt; for all the men who sought to kill you have died.'
translations.20: And Moses took his wife and his sons, and set them upon donkeys, and led them; and he returned to the land of Egypt. And he took the staff which God had commanded him with in his hand.
translations.21: Then God said to him: 'In your going, to return to Egypt — see all the proofs which I have set in your hand: perform them before Pharaoh. And I shall harden his heart, and he shall not let the people go.
translations.22: And say to him: Thus says God in honor: Israel is My son, My firstborn.
translations.23: And I have said to you: Let My son go, that he may worship Me. And if you refuse to let him go — behold, I am about to kill your son, your firstborn.'
translations.24: And it was on the way, at the lodging-place, the angel of God came suddenly upon his son, and sought to kill him.
translations.25: And Zipporah took a flint, and cut off the foreskin of her son, and presented it before [him]; and she said: 'The bridegroom was about to be killed.'
translations.26: And He desisted from him. At that time she said: 'The bridegroom marked for death has become circumcised.'
translations.27: And God said to Aaron: 'Go to meet Moses, into the wilderness.' And he went, and met him at the mountain of God, and kissed him.
translations.28: And Moses informed him of all the words of God which He had sent him with, and all the signs which He had commanded him.
translations.29: And Moses and Aaron went, and gathered all the elders of the sons of Israel.
translations.30: And Aaron spoke all the words which God had spoken to Moses, and performed the wonders in the presence of the people.
translations.31: And the people believed; and when they heard that God had remembered the sons of Israel, and had looked upon their affliction, they bowed down and prostrated themselves.
